lines.text: Do you know how AI image generators work? They don't cut and paste photos. Every picture starts as pure static.
During training, the AI sees millions of pictures. Each one gets buried under random noise, a little more at every step.
Its one job is to look at a noisy picture and guess exactly which noise was added, so it can be taken away.
When you type a prompt, another model turns your words into a long list of numbers that capture their meaning.
Then the generator begins with a screen full of random static.
Step by step, often twenty to fifty times, it removes a little noise, nudged toward your words, until a picture appears.
To save time, many models work on a tiny compressed version of the picture, and only blow it up to full size at the end.
Change the starting static, and you get a different picture. Same static, same words, and you get the same picture again.
So every AI image is sculpted out of noise.
